title: Comfy Fighter Z
subtitle: From a cast file to four arcade games, with ComfyUI
footageDisclosure: Real screen recordings of the generated games, the ComfyUI run graph and the pipeline's own review sheets and logs. The original cast and Rogue Protocol are fictional; Midterm Mayhem 2026 and Billionaires Brawl are satire casts caricatured from text with stock voices. Narration and music are cloud-generated through ComfyUI; nothing was recorded from a person.

voice.deliveryTag: [energetic, confident movie-trailer narration, quick and clear]

scenes.title: Four games, one pipeline
scenes.narration: Four fighting games. Twenty-six fighters. Eight arenas. Every sprite, voice and background here was generated with ComfyUI, from text.
scenes.visualDirection: Hard cuts between live fights in each game, one every two seconds, ending on a super-move cut-in.

scenes.title: It starts with a cast file
scenes.narration: It starts with a cast file: a short description of each fighter, their special move, and the arenas they fight in.
scenes.visualDirection: A code card scrolling slowly through the real cast file, with the fighter fields lit as they are named.

scenes.title: Priced before it runs
scenes.narration: One command prices the entire run before anything is spent, and refuses to run without an approved budget.
scenes.visualDirection: A terminal card typing the prepare command and printing the real estimate lines; the approval line lands last.

scenes.title: One ComfyUI graph
scenes.narration: The run is one ComfyUI graph: character factories, nine-cell sprite sheets, arenas, menus, intro clips, voices and music. Every node calls a cloud model, submitted one paid node at a time.
onScreen: character factories → sprite sheets → arenas → media → audio
scenes.visualDirection: The real run graph in the ComfyUI editor: a wide establishing view, then camera moves across the character column, the sprite-sheet nodes, an environment factory, the media nodes and the audio bank.

scenes.title: Review, then redraw one node
scenes.narration: Contact sheets flag what needs another pass. Only that node is redrawn, so a fix costs cents, not a new run. Here, four sweeps were redrawn until they connected low.
onScreen: reroll one node · the cache keeps the rest
scenes.visualDirection: Slow pans across the real review grids: a fighter's pose sheet, the flagged sweep cells before and after, and the redrawn super cut-ins.

scenes.title: Living stage scenery
scenes.narration: A vision model plans living stage scenery, paints it, separates it into layers, and the game animates them behind the fight.
scenes.visualDirection: The scenery review image with its labelled boxes dissolving into the same arena live in the game, elements moving.

scenes.title: Strict export, one menu
scenes.narration: A strict export checks every file and clip, then every game lands on one GAME SELECT screen with its own title card.
scenes.visualDirection: The export log's passing checks, then the GAME SELECT screen with the five generated title cards and the cursor moving across them.

scenes.title: Ultra Dream Match
scenes.narration: Combine them and you get Ultra Dream Match: all twenty-six fighters, all eight arenas, one final boss. Play it now at comfy-fight-z dot dhaakon dot com, and build your own from the repository.
scenes.captionText: Combine them and you get Ultra Dream Match: all twenty-six fighters, all eight arenas, one final boss. Play it now at comfy-fight-z.dhaakon.com, and build your own from the repository.
scenes.visualDirection: The Ultra select grid, a crossover fight, the final battle, then the end card holding the live and repository addresses.
